contract: Admitted notification triggers deliver one Apprise payload per enabled subscription of the event, render the templates from the trigger data, record the firing or the failed attempt in the settings document and disable a record at maxFailedAttempts; an unusable configuration or a trigger without an active subscription delivers nothing.
exceptions: initial, repeat, changed and failure facets are covered by the listed scenarios.

force is not applicable: the delivery flow has no force mode of its own; the only override is the test route's fail query, characterized by route-r165 and the notifications_updated fail-override scenarios.

The real trigger is the scheduler path: a stub RSS feed with a future publication date, a cron expression with a seconds field and a local episode download, because the new-episode route passes isAutoDownload false and never notifies (server/managers/PodcastManager.js:425).
Delivery to multiple urls in one payload is proven by the payload urls array; Apprise itself is stubbed, so provider-specific fan-out is out of scope.

invariants.contract: An admitted trigger posts one Apprise payload {urls, title, body} per enabled subscription of that event, with title and body rendered from the trigger data (the scheduler trigger uses the downloaded episode and its library item), and records numTimesFired plus one, lastFiredAt and no failed attempt in the settings document and its row.

A trigger with no active subscription for its event posts nothing and leaves the records without a firing, also on the scheduler path where the manager returns before the queue and the emitter while the episode is still stored; with no Apprise URL configured the trigger answers 200, posts nothing and leaves the settings document and its row untouched.

A non-2xx Apprise answer increments numConsecutiveFailedAttempts, sets lastAttemptFailed and lastFiredAt and keeps the record enabled until the count reaches maxFailedAttempts, at which point the record is stored with enabled false and later triggers attempt no delivery; a successful attempt clears the consecutive count and lastAttemptFailed.
